correctness.rationale: The six prime factorial valuation vectors form a unimodular basis; all 2! through 16! reduce to eight atoms. A product equality in the positive integer monoid is precisely equality of six integer coordinates. The two exact binomial relations orient to strictly decrease lexicographic (r,a4+a6), and every irreducible factorization has the unique (r,t)=(max(0,-c3),min(c4,c6)). Hence the two moves generate every equality, and are minimal by the rank-two relation lattice. The semigroup algebra is a height-two binomial complete intersection. Every move changes atomic length by two and has catenary distance four; 14!5! has precisely two disjoint length-two/four factorizations. The coefficient feasibility bounds yield the exact count and set-of-lengths endpoints. The package verifier independently enumerated 9,556 distinct products and 10,008 factorizations up to 10^20 and checked all formulas; no finite enumeration is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Factorization congruences, length sets, delta sets, and catenary degrees are structural invariants of nonunique-factorization monoids. The 13-smooth Jordan–Pólya stratum is the first natural prime-support layer where unique prime-factorial representations break; a two-relation complete intersection with uniform catenary degree 4 is a concrete, all-element classification absent from the preceding membership and counting theorems. This is not an arbitrary finite cutoff or a table recomputation; it describes every product in an infinite natural semigroup.
